RagShortTexts: The economic sustenance of Anteans in 374 AD relied upon extensive agrarian estates, pastoral herds, and strategic mineral extraction.
Anchored around commercial hubs near Middle Dnieper & Dniester Forest, merchant caravans traded valuable bullion, grain, wine, and exotic raw goods.
Advanced weapon smithies and metallurgical workshops provided the industrial backbone necessary to equip large armies in the field.

Variants.Content: Underpinning the immense martial demands of Anteans was an agrarian and mercantile economic system rooted in rural estates and municipal workshops. Across fertile valleys and pastures, countless tenant farmers and laborers produced wheat harvests, vintage wines, cured pelts, and high-grade iron ingots destined for storehouses. Within thriving market plazas around Middle Dnieper & Dniester Forest, cosmopolitan merchants converged to barter gold coinage, imported silks, fine armaments, and livestock. Imperial or royal customs officials maintained toll gates, extracting heavy excise duties from freight wagons. Yet the system faced constant vulnerability from harvest failures and trade route disruptions, compelling rulers to enforce grain requisitions to sustain armies in the field.

Frontier spearmen of Antae haul their mail through spring floods while the cook's kettle stays empty. Each night the sergeant walks the lines to count who still carries a sword and who has sold his belt for bread. Grain pay runs late again, so men wrap their feet in rags and wait for the next convoy to splash across the ford.

Your steward reports that cured pelts and iron ingots sell well in the river towns, yet tolls at the bridge have doubled under the new charter. Lend coin to the wine merchants only through a trusted agent, since an open loan invites a rival to claim a share of the profit. The tenth from our fields is due before midsummer.
